content.title: About
content.content: Coffee cake is a moist, tender cake flavored with ground coffee and often topped with a cream cheese or chocolate glaze. Made with yeast type 2439, it rises during baking, giving it a light, airy crumb. It is commonly served for breakfast, as a snack, or as a dessert with tea.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coffee cake is a staple in many cafés as a lighter alternative to richer desserts.
Yeast type 2439 is selected for sweet doughs, providing consistent rise and a soft texture.
Ground coffee not only adds aroma but also enhances the flavor of chocolate glazes.
In some regions the cake is decorated with nuts, berries, or caramel crumbs.
A gluten‑free version can be made by substituting wheat flour with a gluten‑free blend.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, increasing alertness and concentration.

items.title: Probiotic‑like properties of yeast
items.content: Live yeast can support gut microbiota, although it is usually killed during baking.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast provides B1, B2, B3, and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Coffee cake offers plant protein from flour and yeast, contributing to satiety.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: People sensitive to caffeine may experience nervousness, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Coffee cake is often sweet; excessive sugar intake can lead to weight gain and tooth decay.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, making the cake unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: If the cake is topped with nuts, potential allergic reactions must be considered.

items.title: Yeast temperature shock
items.content: Overly hot ingredients can kill the yeast, resulting in poor rise.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve coffee cake warm or at room temperature, often alongside a cup of coffee or tea. Slice into portions, drizzle with extra glaze, add berries or whipped cream. It pairs well with ice cream, yogurt, or fruit sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. Refrigerate for up to 5 days for longer freshness. Freeze in freezer‑safe bags for up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature before serving.
